function: Distributed noncoherent joint-transmission beamforming at multi-antenna small-cell BSs: DDPG agents learn power and direction parameters of a derived optimal beamforming structure to maximize sum rate (p. 2, 6-7).
system: 12 small-cell BSs with 8-antenna ULAs serve 4 single-antenna UEs in a shared 10 MHz band; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 9).
method: Multi-agent DDPG, one actor-critic agent per SBS (two hidden layers), trained online by reinforcement learning on local CSI and UE feedback; actions set the optimal-structure parameters (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: path loss exponent 4, Rayleigh fading with Gauss-Markov time correlation, UEs in a 200 m radius region; no standard channel model or measurements (p. 3, 8-9).
test_conditions: Online training at J=12, K=4; UE positions redrawn at slot 60000 with continued training (about 6000 slots); SBS count reduced from 12 to 8 without retraining (p. 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned: InAp optimization [25], KKT, KKT-FD, RZF, RZF-Greedy, MRT-Greedy. Learned: MRT-DQN [37], the authors' earlier scheme; DDNJT-FP is a variant of the proposed scheme (p. 8-9).
metrics: Sum rate (bps/Hz) versus time slot, users, SBSs, transmit antennas and channel-estimation reliability; information overhead in scalars; average running time (p. 9-12).
complexity: Average running time 1.31 ms for DDNJT versus 14.83 s for InAp (K=4, J=10, Nt=8), about 0.1%; information overhead 2KNt+3K scalars (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 3: "Rayleigh fading vector from SBS j to UE k at time slot t"; path loss exponent 4 and 200 m region (p. 8-9); custom simulator, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "the proposed scheme can directly adapt to shifts of the number of SBSs without necessitating retraining"; p. 11: "all UEs are randomly generated again at the 60000th time slot, and the SBSs continue to train their network following the previous training process"
q3_support: p. 8: "MRT-DQN [37]: Each SBS employs MRT beamforming and DQN-based power allocation scheme"; p. 8: "InAp [25]: All SBSs use global CSI to collaboratively optimize beamforming vectors to maximize the sum rate"; sum rate compared in Figs. 3-6 (p. 9-11).
q4_support: p. 9: "the running time of the DDNJT scheme is about 0.1% of that of the InAp scheme"; Table II (p. 10) lists 1.31 ms for DDNJT and 14.83 s for InAp.
q5_support: p. 8: "The proposed DDNJT scheme was executed using tensorflow (Version 2.0) and Python (Version 3.8)"; no code or data link is given and the channels are simulated.
notes: Area 3: DDPG agents set the power factors and Lagrange multipliers that build each small-cell BS precoder in a MISO system; no RIS (RIS appears only in related work and future work, p. 2, 12). q2 rests on the generalization section: abrupt UE-position change handled by continued training (about 6000 slots against 40000 for initial convergence) and a drop from 12 to 8 SBSs without retraining (p. 11-12). The figure legends cite InAp as [21] and MRT-DQN as [33], while the text cites [25] and [37].
